description: We’re a team of teenagers who think space shouldn’t feel out of reach. We built ARTEMIS 4 so anyone can try what it takes to plan, fund and fly a Moon mission, no background needed.
summary: We have developed an original videogame detailing three main aspects of a space mission: budgeting, construction of the spaceship and astronaut experience. Our objective was to bring a youthful and fun approach to space missions, since as youths ourselves, we had a different view and a closer perspective about what teenagers/kids enjoy about mixing STEM and games than many adults could have.
details:
Our video game covers three of the main parts of a space mission. First of all, budgeting. As teenagers ourselves who more than once have had to negotiate a couple euros to go grab some food with friends, we approsched space mission budgets in that way, an approschable way that teenagers would understand. In the first part of the game, the player acts as a NASA financial advisor of sorts, disscussing and trying to convince different investors, which are AI, on how their mission will be important for humanity, how taxpayers will react to the costs and how much money they are asking. The player can either choose already created text options or, if they like a challenge, text the answers themselves. The AI have been trained with NASA data bases, and a specific panel with budgeting/ space mission related costs is available to the player before and during the argument section. This way, teenagers can learn about the costs associated to space missions in a fun way. Next to each investor is a bar, that shows the level of satisfaction of the judges, and this changes depending on how the player answers. At the end of the section, taking in account the satisfaction levels a total budget is allocated.

The second section involves construction of the spaceship. The player engages in a sort of shop inside a NASA lab, where depending on the budget they achieved in part 1 they can buy a series of spaceship parts, tools and other things astronauts pack when going on a space mission. Depending on how successfully the player completed part 1 they can buy more/less things from the shop, and the things the player chooses to buy impact the third section of the video game. In the shop, every product comes with the price, and description, which helps players learn more about the different things astronauts bring on their voyage. Products and spaceship parts were all inspired or taken from real NASA missions or models, information we obtained from databases.

Section three of the game involves a series of mini games. First of all, the player engages in a sort of angry birds-like minigame, where they decide the trajectory and power of the launch. In this part, they player can see the fuel the spaceship has, altitude and speed, data also obtained from NASA databases. Afterwards, the player engages in three mini games: fixing a specific issue on the spaceship and maintaining the trajectory in case of an emergency, a classic asteroid dodging game, where the player learns about space debris, and fixing the spaceship’s water tank. All of these problems either teach the player about an anstronaut’s voyage in space or are based on real issues astronauts have faced on the past. Only if the player correctly completes 2 out of the three challenges do they get to land. After a final minigame where they land a moon lander with a design inspired by real NASA moon landers do they complete the final mission. Also, while on the voyage, curious facts about astronauts and space missions display on screen.

The player, if they fail any section they try again that specific section (1, 2 or 3).

This game was made as a joined effort by a group of friends with very diverse talents. 3 of the team members were in charge of coding, and used both Gemini and Claude to code the game in C++. All code generated by Claude was proofread by the team. The other two members were in charge of creative direction and design. Backgrounds and characters are all origininal and were created manually with pixelart. Most items as well, although some complex items, like the moon lander, were created by Gemini, taking inspiration from real NASA moon landers. Storyline is completely original. It came from our main mission when approaching this hackathon. How could we create a game that is both enjoyed by kids and teens and teaches them about NASA and space missions? We want to make an impact by sharing our love for space with other teenagers and kids, encouraging anyone, no matter their age or where they’re from to pursue their love and interest about space. Although we did take inspiration from existing games, like Among Us and angry birds for specific areas of our game, we tried to be as creative as we could, to create the most entertaining game possible. As a team, we’re extreme,y proud of what we’ve created, and we think this game can make a positive effect on many children and teenagers and maybe even adults. Space is fun, and we wanted to reflect that every step of the way.
